tune:
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: Aggressively explore static_v gate vectors of gated_fno under TWO new constraints that distinguish this run from the parallel SDSC run: (a) linear frequency binning instead of log-spaced, and (b) an OPEN bias (mean of static_v must be >= 0.5). The goal is to characterize how the model behaves when the gating spectrum is uniformly mapped AND the FNO is required to process at least half of the spectrum on average.

MANDATORY CONSTRAINTS (do not violate):
1. Set gate_mapping = "linear" in EVERY round. Do not vary gate_mapping in this run. Do not fall back to the default "log" — even though the model description recommends log for TIDMAD physics, this run is specifically testing the linear binning. Plans with gate_mapping="log" defeat the purpose of this run.
2. Set gate_step = 0.1 in every round (same as the SDSC parallel run, so gate_mapping is the only frequency-related variable that differs).
3. **mean(static_v) MUST be >= 0.5 in every round.** That is: (sum of all static_v entries) / num_gates >= 0.5. This rules out 'mostly-closed' shapes (e.g. low-pass with cutoff at gate index 16 of 128, which would have mean ~0.125). It permits balanced shapes, smooth ramps centered above 0.5, soft attenuations, and 'mostly-open' shapes. Before submitting any plan, compute the mean of your proposed static_v and verify it is >= 0.5. If it isn't, redesign the shape — add more high values or shift the open region to cover more of the spectrum.
4. Every round MUST use a static_v shape that is meaningfully DIFFERENT from every previous round in this run. Track what you have already tried. Repeating the same shape (or trivial perturbations of it) is forbidden.
5. static_v entries must lie on the discrete grid {0.0, 0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0}. The pydantic validator will reject anything else.
6. DO NOT only try binary {0, 1} masks. Use intermediate values (0.1 through 0.9) to build smooth curves. At least 70% of the rounds in this run must use static_v vectors that contain at least three distinct values from the grid.
7. Other model_config fields (width, num_layers, num_gates) and train_config fields (lr, epochs, batch_size, optimizer) should stay close to their defaults across rounds. Do NOT waste rounds tuning them — the only intentional variable in this run is static_v. (gate_mapping and gate_step are pinned by constraints 1-2.)

COMPUTING THE MEAN — examples (gate_step=0.1, num_gates=128):
- All-1.0 vector: mean = 1.0 ✓ (passes)
- All-0.5 vector: mean = 0.5 ✓ (passes — this is the boundary)
- All-0.0 vector: mean = 0.0 ✗ (fails — pure identity, no denoising)
- Low-pass with [1.0]*16 + [0.0]*112: mean = 0.125 ✗ (fails — too closed)
- High-pass with [0.0]*16 + [1.0]*112: mean = 0.875 ✓ (passes — mostly open)
- Balanced: [0.6]*128: mean = 0.6 ✓ (passes)
- Symmetric ramp [1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, ...]: depends on length, compute it

SHAPES TO EXPLORE (mean >= 0.5 versions — cover several families, do not repeat):
- High-pass with varying cutoff: e.g. [0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, ...] — engages AI on most frequencies, protects only the lowest. Mean is high.
- Mostly-open with soft notch: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.0, ...] — full processing except a soft dip in one band.
- Graded full-spectrum processing: [0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, ...] — every gate is at least half-engaged.
- Mild attenuation everywhere: [0.7]*128 or [0.8]*64 + [0.6]*64 — mean is well above 0.5, gating is softer everywhere.
- High-pass + boost band: [0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.0, ...] — protects low freqs softly while emphasizing a mid-band.
- Comb / multi-band with bias toward high values: [0.6, 1.0, 0.6, 1.0, 0.6, 1.0, ...] — alternating but never below 0.5.
- Soft attenuation in two narrow notches: mostly 1.0 with two small dips to 0.2 — mean ~0.95.

CONTEXT FOR WHY THIS RUN EXISTS:
- A previous gated_fno run (small_sample_trial_v1) only tried 2 distinct static_v shapes — both binary {0,1} masks, biased toward closed. The best score came from a low-pass binary mask with mean ~0.125 (very closed).
- A parallel run on SDSC (static_v_focused_v1) tests exhaustive enumeration of shape families with log gate_mapping and no mean constraint.
- This run tests the OPPOSITE bias: linear gate_mapping (uniform binning instead of log) AND a forced 'open' bias (mean >= 0.5). The hypothesis: maybe the previous run failed not just because it picked binary masks, but because it picked CLOSED binary masks. Forcing the model to process more of the spectrum may reveal whether the FNO architecture is being underutilized when too many gates are zeroed.
- After this run, we will compare: distinct shapes per run (diversity), mean(static_v) distribution per run (open vs closed bias), and best score per run (does open bias help or hurt?). The contrast is one-axis-at-a-time: same model, same max_rounds, same trial mode, same defaults — only gate_mapping and the mean constraint differ.

SELF-CHECK BEFORE EVERY PLAN: (1) Is gate_mapping = "linear"? (2) Is gate_step = 0.1? (3) Does mean(static_v) >= 0.5? (4) Is this static_v shape different from every previous round? (5) Does it have at least 3 distinct values? If any answer is no, redesign the plan.
